style_when: the article is a purely conceptual synthesis or policy dilemma where no physical facility, machine, or supply chain exists, and an elegant abstract paper silhouette states the idea. Never reach for paper collage when the story describes physical manufacturing, freight, energy, hardware, or heavy infrastructure — use cinematic still or telephoto industry instead
prompt: Editorial cut-paper collage on a warm oak desk in a home study. Split-screen diptych with a clean vertical seam of torn paper fibre. LEFT HALF: a large graphite-grey rag-paper cloud silhouette hovers, tethered by a taut cut-paper chain down to a small bone-white paper house, the chain fused to the roof. RIGHT HALF: the same bone-white paper house stands free, a single open chain link of ochre paper resting unclipped on the desk beside it, the cloud gone. Hand-torn rag paper with visible fibre, crisp cut edges, deep physical cast shadows under every layer, generous negative space. One raking light from the upper left, palette of bone white, graphite and ochre. No legible print.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, legible print
rationale: The story turns on a rename and a pricing philosophy, not a facility — a conceptual synthesis where no literal machine carries it. Cut-paper silhouettes of a house, a cloud and a chain link state 'cloud becomes link' at a glance, and the fused-versus-unclipped chain enacts the article's exact contrast: required big-tech rent versus optional, no-lock-in service.
cue: Home Assistant Cloud becomes Home Assistant Link
subject: a cut-paper house chained to a paper cloud on one half, freed beside an unclipped paper link on the other
core_thesis: Cloud access has become a recurring rent on hardware people already own — and the honest counterweight is not 'self-hosting is free' but a maintenance bill that is itself being repriced.
core_conflict: The walled, required big-tech cloud that taxes devices you already bought versus an optional, unclippable service where the cash bill is merely swapped for a bill paid in hours, hardware and cert renewals.
composition: split-screen diptych with a clean vertical torn-fibre seam; left half the locked tether, right half the freed link, hero silhouettes off-centre with generous negative space
